name: The Double Check
summary: A knight and rook check the king at once; a double check can only be met by a king move, and here there is none, so it is mate.
intro: A double check is the most forcing move in all of chess. Two pieces attack the king simultaneously, and no capture or block can neutralize both at the same time, so the king is legally required to move. When the king has no flight square, a double check becomes instant checkmate regardless of how much material the defender may hold.
boardCaption: White plays Ng6#, the knight checking the king on h8 while unveiling the rook on e8's check along the eighth rank for a double check.

sections.heading: The Motif
paragraphs: A double check occurs when a piece moves to give check while simultaneously revealing check from another piece behind it. Because two attackers strike at once, the defender cannot block both lines with one interposition, nor capture both checking pieces in a single move. The only legal reply is to move the king.

This makes the double check uniquely forcing: material counts for nothing, blocking is impossible, and even a queen on the board offers no help. If every square around the king is covered or occupied, the double check ends the game on the spot. Spotting one is often the difference between a draw and a brilliant mate.

sections.heading: The Line
paragraphs: White delivers 1.Ng6#. The knight lands on g6 and attacks the black king on h8, while its departure from f8 opens the eighth rank so the rook on e8 also checks the king. Two pieces give check at the same instant, so Black must move the king and cannot block or capture his way out.

But the king on h8 has nowhere to go: its own pawns on g7 and h7 wall it in, and g6 is occupied by the checking knight. With no legal king move available, the double check is checkmate. It makes no difference that Black has an extra queen sitting on a5, since material is powerless against a double check.

keyIdeas: A double check attacks the king with two pieces at once.
It cannot be met by blocking or by a capture.
The king is forced to move, no matter the material.
Here Ng6 checks while unveiling the rook on the eighth rank.
The king on h8 has no escape square available.
With no legal move, the double check is checkmate.
